And they will be mine,” says the Lord of hosts, “on the day when I act, as my possession; and I will spare them, as a man spares his son who serves him. “Turn” [Note: [Col. 0932] The sacred Bibles have: “You will turn.”] “and see what is between the just and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who does not serve him.”

[IV.] “For behold, the day will come, burning like a furnace, and all the proud and all who do iniquity will be stubble. And the coming day will set them on fire, says the Lord of hosts, which will leave them neither root nor shoot. But for you who fear my name the sun of justice will rise, and healing in its wings; and you will go forth and leap like calves from the herd. And you will tread down the wicked, when they are ashes beneath the soles of your feet, on the day when I act, says the Lord of hosts.”

## THE BOOK OF ISAIAH

[Chapter I.] “Wash yourselves, be clean; remove the evil of your thoughts from my sight. Cease to act perversely; learn to do good; seek judgment; help the oppressed; judge the orphan; defend the widow. And come and bring your case against me, says the Lord.”

And eight verses later: “Your silver has become dross; your wine has been mixed with water. Your princes are companions of thieves; they all love gifts and pursue rewards. They do not judge the orphan, and the widow’s case does not come before them.”

And a little later [II]: “House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord. For you have cast away your people, the house of Jacob, because they have been filled as formerly, and have had diviners like the Philistines, and have clung to foreign children.”

And three verses later: “His land has been filled with idols; they worshiped the work of their hands, which their fingers made.”

And five verses later: “For the day of the Lord of hosts is against every proud and lofty person, and against everyone who is arrogant, and he will be humbled.”

And a little later [III]: “My people have been despoiled by their exactors, and women have ruled over them. My people, those who call you blessed have deceived you, and have destroyed the way of your steps.”

And several verses later: “For you have ravaged my vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your house. Why do you crush my people and grind the faces of the poor?” says the Lord of hosts.

And the Lord said: “Because the daughters of Zion have been lifted up, and have walked with outstretched necks, going with glances of the eyes, clapping and walking, and proceeding on their feet with measured step.”

And shortly afterward [V]: “Woe to those who join house to house and attach field to field, right up to the furthest limit of the place” [Note: [Col. 0933] The Royal Manuscript reads, “up to the boundaries of the place”; the Vulgate, however, “up to the boundary of the place.” Moreover, that same codex, together with the Vulgate, likewise lacks these words, “so that you may remove your neighbor”; these words were added from the Septuagint, not without a copyist’s error. It is permissible to suppose that the little annotation was inserted here either by Augustine or by someone else from Jerome’s Commentaries, where he observes this concerning the passage: “For what we said, ‘up to the boundary of the place,’ the Septuagint translated *hina tou plēsion aphēlōntai ti*—that is, ‘so that they may take something away from their neighbor’; Symmachus and Theodotion translated, ‘until it fails,’ or ‘there is no place’—so that, when the land has failed, greed may in no way be satisfied.”] (“so that you may remove your neighbor”; Symmachus and Theodotion translated it, “until it fails,” or “there is no place”): “Will you alone dwell in the midst of the earth? These things are in my ears,” says the Lord of hosts.

And three verses later: “Woe to those who rise early to pursue drunkenness and drink until evening, so that they may be inflamed with wine. Harp, lyre, tambourine, flute, and wine are in your banquets; but you do not regard the work of the Lord, nor consider the works of his hands.”

And seventeen verses later: “Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who make darkness light and light darkness, who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter. Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and prudent in their own estimation. Woe to those who are mighty at drinking wine and strong men at mixing drunkenness, who justify the wicked for gifts and take away the justice of the righteous from him.”

And somewhat later [X]: “Woe to those who draw up unjust laws and, when writing, write injustice, in order to oppress the poor in judgment and do violence to the cause of the humble among my people, so that widows may become their spoil and they may plunder orphans.”

And shortly afterward [XI]: “The spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and strength, the spirit of knowledge and piety; and the spirit of the fear of the Lord shall fill him. He shall not judge according to the sight of his eyes, nor reprove according to the hearing of his ears; but he shall judge the poor with justice and reprove the meek of the earth with equity. He shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked. Justice shall be the belt of his loins, and faith the girdle of his kidneys.”

And sixty verses later [XII]: “Behold, God is my savior; I shall act confidently and shall not fear. For the Lord God is my strength and my praise, and he has become my salvation. You shall draw water with joy from the fountains of the Savior; and on that day you shall say: ‘Give thanks to the Lord and invoke his name; make his works known among the peoples; remember that his name is exalted. Sing to the Lord, for he has done magnificently; announce this throughout all the earth. Rejoice and praise, O dwelling of Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.’”

And forty verses later [XIII]: “And I shall make the pride of the faithless cease, and I shall humble the arrogance of the strong.”

Again, somewhat later [XVII]: “The Lord God of Israel says: On that day a man shall bow down to his Maker, and his eyes shall look toward the Holy One of Israel; he shall not bow down to the altars that his hands have made, nor to the things that his fingers have fashioned; he shall not look upon the sacred groves or shrines.”

And somewhat later [XXII]: “The Lord God of hosts shall call, he says, on that day to weeping and mourning, to baldness and the wearing of sackcloth. And behold, joy and gladness: killing calves, slaughtering rams, eating meat, and drinking wine. ‘Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall die.’ And the voice of the Lord of hosts was revealed in my ears: ‘This iniquity shall not be forgiven you until you die,’ says the Lord God of hosts.”

Again, somewhat later [XXVI]: “Open the gates, and let the righteous nation enter, the one keeping faithfulness. The old error has passed away; you will preserve peace—peace, because we have hoped in you. Hope in the Lord forever and ever, in the Lord God, the strong one, forever.”

And six verses later: “On the path of your judgments, O Lord, we have waited for you; your name and your remembrance are the desire of the soul. My soul desired you in the night; indeed, with my spirit within me I shall watch for you from morning onward. When you execute your judgments on the earth, the inhabitants of the earth shall learn righteousness. Let us have mercy on the wicked, and he will not learn to practice justice. In the land of the saints he has acted wickedly, and he shall not see the glory of God.”

And somewhat later [XXIX]: “He who prevailed has failed; the mocker has been finished; and all who kept watch over iniquity, who made people sin by their word, have been cut down.”

And ten verses later [XXX]: “Woe, rebellious children, says the Lord, that you might make a plan—and not from me—and weave a web—and not by my spirit—in order to add sin upon sin.”

And shortly afterward: “Thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel: If you return and rest, you shall be saved. In silence and in hope shall be your strength; but you were unwilling.”

And twenty verses later: “You will defile the plates of your silver carvings and the garment of your gold casting, and you will scatter them like a menstruating woman’s impurity.”

And somewhat later [XXXI]: “Return, as you had withdrawn into the deep, O children of Israel. For on that day a man shall cast away the idols of his silver and the idols of his gold, which your hands made for you as a sin.”

Again, somewhat later [XXXIII]: “And there shall be faithfulness in your times, the riches of salvation, wisdom and knowledge; the fear of the Lord itself is his treasure.”

And shortly afterward: “Who among you will be able to dwell with consuming fire? Who among you will dwell with everlasting burnings? The one who walks in righteousness and speaks truth; who casts away greed and slander” [Note: [Col. 0935] The Vulgate version has “from slander.” The Syriac and Arabic have “and oppression.” The Septuagint has “and injustice.”], “and shakes his hands free from every gift; who stops his ears so as not to hear of bloodshed, and closes his eyes so as not to see every” [Note: [Col. 0935] “Every” is absent from the sacred text in the Bibles.] “evil. He shall dwell in the heights; the lofty places of rocks shall be his refuge. His bread shall be given to him, and his waters shall be sure.”

And somewhat later [XLIV]: “Remember these things, O Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I formed you; you are my servant, Israel; do not forget me. I have wiped away your iniquities like a cloud and your sins like a mist. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.”

Again, somewhat later [XLVI]: “Remember this and be ashamed; return, transgressors, to your heart. Remember the former age, for I am God, and there is no other god, nor is there anyone like me.”

And somewhat later [L]: “Who walked” [Note: [Col. 0935] The Sacred Bible reads, “who walked”; Jerome interprets this of Christ: “Who did not have form,” he says, “nor glory, but in the likeness of sinful flesh he assumed the form of a servant.” Nevertheless, Augustine appears to have read, “who walked,” and to have understood it of a person acting amid the darkness of his sins.] “in darkness and has no light? Let him hope in the name of the Lord and rely upon his God.”

Again, somewhat later [LI]: “Hear me, you who know righteousness, a people” [Note: [Col. 0935] The Vulgate has “my people.” “My” is absent from the Hebrew and from the ancient Corbie Bibles, as well as from all the printed editions and manuscripts of this work.], “whose law is in their hearts. Do not fear the reproaches of men, and do not be afraid of their blasphemies. For just as a garment, so the worm shall eat them; and just as wool, so the moth shall devour them. But my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness from generation to generation.”

And somewhat later [LV]: “Seek the Lord while he may be found; call upon him while he is near. Let the wicked abandon his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts, and let him return to the Lord; and he will have mercy on him, and to our God, for he is abundant in forgiveness.”

And twenty verses later [LVI]: “Thus says the Lord: Keep judgment and practice righteousness, because my salvation is near to come and my righteousness to be revealed. Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who embraces it, keeping the sabbath so as not to profane it, keeping his hands so as not to do any evil.”

And not long afterward [LVII]: “You who find consolation in gods beneath every leafy tree, sacrificing children in the torrents, beneath prominent” [Note: [Col. 0935] The printed editions have “overhanging.” But the manuscripts, in accordance with the Vulgate, have “jutting out.”] “rocks: in the regions of the torrent is your portion. This is your lot; and to them you offered” [Col. 0936] “a libation” [Note: [Col. 0936] The Vulgate has “you poured out a libation.”]; “you offered a sacrifice. Shall I not be angry over these things?”

Again, somewhat later [LVIII]: “For they seek me day after day and desire to know my ways, like a nation that has practiced righteousness and has not abandoned the judgment of its God. They ask me for judgments of righteousness; they desire to draw near to God. ‘Why have we fasted, and you did not look upon us? We humbled our souls, and you did not know?’ Behold, on the day of your fast your will is found, and you exact payment from all your debtors. Behold, you fast for disputes and quarrels, and you strike with the fist wickedly. Do not fast as you have done until this day, so that your outcry may be heard on high. Is this the fast that I have chosen: for a day to afflict a man’s soul? Is it to bend his head down like a circle and spread sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast and a day acceptable to the Lord? Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen? Break the bonds of wickedness; undo the bundles that oppress. Set free those who are broken, as free persons, and break every burden. Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house. When you see the naked, clothe him, and do not despise your own flesh.”

And four verses later [Note: [Col. 0936] The Royal Manuscript has “after three verses.” The printed editions have “after the fourth”; perhaps this should read “after four.” The same applies somewhat below, where it now reads “And after six verses”; the printed editions had “And after the sixth verse”; the Royal Manuscript, “And after seven verses.”]: “If you remove from your midst the chain, and cease to point the finger and to speak what is useless; if you pour out your soul for the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, your light shall rise in darkness, and your darkness shall be like midday; and the Lord shall give you rest always.”

And after many passages [LXV]: “A people who provoke me to anger are always before my face, who sacrifice in gardens and offer sacrifices upon bricks, who dwell in tombs and sleep in the shrines of idols.”

And two verses later: “Who say, ‘Withdraw from me; do not come near me, for you are unclean.’ These shall be smoke in my anger, a fire burning all day. Behold, it is written before me: I shall not be silent, but I shall repay and recompense into their bosom your iniquities and the iniquities of your fathers together,” says the Lord. “Those who sacrificed upon the mountains and hills reproached me, and I shall measure out their former work into their bosom.”

And ten verses later: “And you,” he says, “who have abandoned the Lord, who have forgotten my holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and pour libations upon it: I shall number you by the sword, and all of you shall fall in slaughter, because I called and you did not answer; I spoke and you did not listen; you did evil in my eyes and chose what I did not desire.”

And shortly afterward [LXVI]: “Thus says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet. What is this house that you will build for me, and what is this place of my rest? My hand made all these things, and all these things came to be,” says the Lord. “But upon whom shall I look, except upon the poor man, the contrite in spirit, and the one who trembles at my words?”

And six verses later: [Col. 0937] “I shall choose their mockeries, and I shall bring upon them the things they feared, because I called and there was no one who answered; I spoke and they did not hear. They did evil in my eyes and chose what I did not desire. Hear the law of the Lord, you who tremble at his word. Your brothers who hate you and cast you out for the sake of my name said, ‘Let the Lord be glorified, and we shall see your joy’; but they themselves shall be put to shame.”

## From the Book of Jeremiah

[Chapter II] Hear the word of the Lord, O house of Jacob and all the families of the house of Israel. Thus says the Lord: “What injustice did your fathers find in me, that they went far from me and walked after vanity and became vain?”

And ten verses later: “You have made my inheritance an abomination. The priests did not say, ‘Where is the Lord?’ Those who held the law did not know me; the shepherds transgressed against me; the prophets prophesied by Baal; and they followed idols.”

And shortly afterward: “Will a virgin forget her ornament, or a bride her breast-band? But my people have forgotten me for innumerable days. Why do you strive to display your good way in seeking love, when you have even taught your ways to do evil? And the blood of the souls of the poor and innocent has been found on your wings. I did not find them in pits, but in all the things mentioned above. And you said, ‘I am without sin and innocent; therefore let your anger turn away from me.’ Behold, I shall contend with you in judgment, because you said, ‘I have not sinned.’ How utterly vile you have become, repeating your ways! And you shall be put to shame by Egypt, just as you were put to shame by Assyria. For you shall also depart from there, and your hands shall be upon your head, because the Lord has crushed your confidence.”

And shortly afterward [III]: “Return, returning children,” says the Lord, “for I am your husband.”

Again, shortly afterward [IV]: “If you turn back” [Note: [Col. 0937] The Vulgate now reads “if you return”; but in the ancient Corbie Bibles, as here, “if you turn back.”], “Israel,” says the Lord, “turn back to me. If you remove your stumbling blocks from before my face, you shall not be shaken. And you shall swear, ‘The Lord lives,’ in truth, in judgment, and in righteousness; and the nations shall bless him and praise him.”

And shortly afterward: “My foolish people did not know me; they are foolish children and without understanding. They are wise at doing evil, but they did not know how to do good.”

And thirty verses later [V]: “Go around the streets of Jerusalem, look and consider, and seek in its squares whether you can find a man practicing judgment and seeking faithfulness, and I shall be merciful to him. But even if they say, ‘As the Lord lives,’ they will swear falsely. Lord, your eyes look upon faithfulness. You struck them, and they did not grieve; you crushed them, and they refused to accept discipline. They hardened their faces like rock; they did not wish to return.

“But I said, ‘Perhaps they are poor and foolish, ignorant of the way of the Lord, the judgment of their God. I shall go, therefore, to the great men and speak to them; for they know the way of the Lord, the judgment of their God.’ And behold, these too had broken the yoke altogether and torn the bonds.”

And six verses later: “Your children have abandoned me” [Col. 0938], “and swear by those who are not gods. I satisfied them, and they committed adultery; they indulged themselves in the house of a prostitute. They became lustful horses and stallions; each one neighed for his neighbor’s wife. Shall I not visit these things,” says the Lord, “and shall my hand not take vengeance on such a nation?”

And forty verses later: “I appointed sand as a boundary for the sea, an everlasting ordinance that shall not pass away. Its waves shall be shaken, but they shall not prevail; its waves shall swell, but they shall not cross it. But the heart of this people became unbelieving and rebellious; they withdrew and went away, and they did not say in their heart, ‘Let us fear the Lord our God.’”

And a few verses later [Note: [Col. 0938] The Royal Manuscript has “and after seven verses.”]: “The wicked have been found among my people,” he says, “lying in wait like bird-catchers, setting snares and traps to catch men. As a cage full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit; therefore they have become great and prosperous. They have grown fat and sleek, and they have passed beyond my words most wickedly. They did not plead the cause of the orphan” [Note: [Col. 0938] The Vulgate has: “They did not judge the cause of the widow; they did not direct the cause of the orphan.” Jerome likewise has this, except that he omits the word “widow,” which is not in the Hebrew and was added by a second hand in the ancient Corbie Bibles.], “and they did not judge the judgment of the poor. Shall I not visit these things,” says the Lord, “or shall my soul not take vengeance on such a nation?”

[Note: [Col. 0938] Here the following words are inserted in the Royal Manuscript: “Then he explains what he had said above: ‘I shall go to the great men and speak to them; perhaps they know the way of the Lord’; and behold, these have likewise broken the yoke and torn the bonds. Now he describes who the great men are: namely, the prophets and priests, some of whom proclaim future things, while others determine from the Law what must be done. ‘And behold,’ he says, ‘while they were prophesying falsehood, the priests applauded them with their hands.’ And to show that the people are not without blame, since they are led astray by such men, it is written, ‘And my people loved such things’; once mine, but after loving such things it ceases to be mine. What, then, will they do when the final time of judgment arrives—or the necessity of captivity, from which astonishment and marvels have arisen, because neither among the rulers nor among the people was anyone found who thought rightly?” These excerpts are taken from Jerome’s Commentary on Jeremiah.]

“Astonishment and marvels have occurred in the land. The prophets prophesied falsehood, and the priests applauded with their hands, and my people loved such things. What, then, will happen at its end?”

And thirty verses later [VI]: “To whom shall I speak, and whom shall I warn, so that he may hear? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot hear. Behold, the word of the Lord has become a reproach to them, and they do not receive it.”

And shortly afterward [VII]: “Hear the word of the Lord, all Judah, you who enter through these gates to worship the Lord. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Make your ways and your practices good, and I shall dwell with you in this place. Do not trust in words of falsehood, saying, ‘The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord it is.’

“For if you truly direct your ways and your practices, if you practice judgment between a man and his neighbor, if you do not oppress the resident alien, the orphan, or the widow, if you do not shed innocent blood in this place, and if you do not walk after foreign gods to your own harm, I shall dwell with you in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers, from age to age and forever.

“Behold, you trust in yourselves” [Col. 0939] “in words of falsehood that will not profit you: stealing, killing, committing adultery, swearing falsely, making libations to the Baals, and going after foreign gods whom you do not know. Then you came and stood before me in this house in which my name has been invoked, and you said, ‘We have been delivered, because we have committed all these abominations.’ Has this house, in which my name has been invoked, therefore become a cave of thieves in your eyes?” [Note: [Col. 0939] The Vulgate has: “Has it therefore become?”] “I, I am he; I have seen it,” says the Lord.

“Go to my place at Shiloh, where my name dwelt from the beginning, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel. And now, because you have done all these works,” says the Lord, “and I spoke to you, rising early and speaking, but you did not listen; I called, but you did not answer: I shall do to this house in which my name has been invoked, in which you trust, and to the place that I gave to your fathers, just as I did to Shiloh. And I shall cast you away from my face, just as I cast away all your brothers, the whole seed of Ephraim.

“Therefore you must not pray for this people, nor take up praise or prayer on their behalf, nor oppose me, because I shall not hear you. Do you not see what these people are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the queen of heaven; and they pour libations to foreign gods, provoking me to anger. Are they provoking me to anger,” says the Lord, “and not rather themselves, to the shame of their faces?”

And shortly afterward [VIII]: “Will one who falls not rise again? And will one who has turned away not return? Why, then, has this people in Jerusalem turned away with a contentious turning? They have grasped falsehood and did not wish to return. I paid attention and listened; no one speaks what is good. There is no one who repents of his sin, saying, ‘What have I done?’”

And nine verses later: “How can you say, ‘We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us’? Truly, the lying stylus of the scribes has worked falsehood. The wise have been put to shame, terrified, and captured. For they have rejected the word of the Lord, and there is no wisdom in them.”

And shortly afterward [IX]: “Who will give me a lodging for travelers in the wilderness, so that I may leave my people and depart from them? For they are all adulterers, an assembly of transgressors. They have stretched out their tongue like a bow of falsehood and not of truth. They have grown strong in the land, for they have gone from evil to evil, and they have not known me,” says the Lord.

“Let each one guard himself from his neighbor, and let him place no trust in any brother, because every brother will utterly supplant, and every friend will proceed deceitfully. A man will mock his brother, and they will not speak the truth. For they have taught their tongue to speak falsehood; they have labored to act wickedly. Your dwelling is in the midst of deceit. In deceit they refused to know me,” says the Lord.

“Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I shall melt them and test them. For what else shall I do because of the daughter of my people? Their tongue is a wounding arrow” [Col. 0940], “it has spoken deceit from its mouth. He speaks peace with his friend, but secretly sets an ambush. Shall I not visit these things,” says the Lord, “or shall my soul not take vengeance on such a nation?”

And shortly afterward: “Thus says the Lord: Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, let not the strong man glory in his strength, and let not the rich man glory in his riches. But let the one who glories glory in this: that he understands and knows me, that I am the Lord who practices mercy, judgment, and righteousness on the earth. For these things please me,” says the Lord.

And sixteen verses later [X]: “Thus says the Lord: Do not learn the ways of the nations, and do not fear the signs of heaven, which the nations fear, because the laws of the peoples are vain. For a craftsman cuts a tree from the forest, the work of his hands with an axe; he decorates it with silver and gold and fastens it with nails and hammers so that it will not fall apart. They are fashioned in the likeness of a palm tree, and they will not speak; they must be carried, because they cannot walk. Therefore do not fear them, for they can do neither evil nor good.

“There is none like you, O Lord; you are great, and great is your name in strength. Who will not fear you, O King of the nations? For yours is the honor among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms there is none like you. Together they shall be proved foolish and senseless; their teaching of vanities is wood.

“Silver beaten thin is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of the craftsman and the hands of the goldsmith. Hyacinth and purple are their clothing; all these are the work of artisans. But the Lord God is true; he is the living God and the everlasting king. At his indignation the earth shall be shaken, and the nations shall not endure his threat.

“Thus, then, you shall say to them: ‘Let the gods who did not make heaven and earth perish from the earth and from the things beneath heaven.’”

And somewhat later [XVII]: “Thus says the Lord: Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart departs from the Lord. He shall be like a tamarisk in the desert and shall not see good when it comes; he shall dwell in dryness in the desert, in a salt land and uninhabited.

“Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his confidence. He shall be like a tree transplanted beside waters, sending its roots toward moisture. He shall not fear when the heat comes; its leaf shall be green. In a time of drought it shall not be anxious, nor shall it ever cease to bear fruit.”

Again, somewhat later [XXII]: “Thus says the Lord: Practice judgment and righteousness, and deliver the one oppressed by force from the hand of the slanderer; do not grieve or oppress unjustly the resident alien, the orphan, or the widow; and do not shed innocent blood in this place.”

And shortly afterward [XXIII]: “Woe to the shepherds who scatter and tear apart the flock of my pasture,” says the Lord. “Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel to the shepherds who pasture my people: You have scattered my flock, driven them away, and not visited them. Behold, I shall visit upon you the wickedness of your practices,” says the Lord.

Again, shortly afterward: “Thus says the Lord of hosts: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you” [Col. 0941] “and deceive you. They speak the vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of the Lord. They say to those who blaspheme me, ‘The Lord has spoken: peace shall be yours’; and to everyone who walks in the perversity of his heart they say, ‘Evil shall not come upon you.’ For who was present in the council of the Lord?”

And eleven verses later: “I did not send the prophets, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied. If they had stood in my council and made my words known to my people, I would certainly have turned them from their evil way and from their worst thoughts.”

And four verses later: “I heard what the prophets said, prophesying falsehood in my name and saying, ‘I dreamed, I dreamed.’ How long will this be in the heart of the prophets who prophesy falsehood and prophesy the deceptions of their own heart, who intend to make my people forget my name because of the dreams of their heart” [Note: [Col. 0941] The Sacred Bibles have “their dreams.”], “which each one recounts to his neighbor, just as their fathers forgot my name because of Baal?

“Let the prophet who has a dream recount a dream; and let the one who has my word recount my word truthfully. What has straw to do with wheat?” says the Lord. “Are not my words like fire,” says the Lord, “and like a hammer shattering rock?

“Therefore, behold, I am against the prophets,” says the Lord, “who steal my words, each one from his neighbor. Behold, I am against the prophets,” says the Lord, “who take up their tongues and say, ‘The Lord says.’ Behold, I am against the prophets who dream falsehood,” says the Lord, “who recount them and deceive my people by their falsehood and their wonders, although I did not send them or command them; they have profited this people nothing,” says the Lord.

And shortly afterward [XXV]: “The Lord sent to you all his servants, the prophets, rising early and sending them; but you did not listen, nor incline your ears to hear, when he said: ‘Return, each one, from his evil way and from your worst thoughts, and you shall dwell in the land that the Lord gave to you and to your fathers, from age to age and forever. Do not go after foreign gods to serve and worship them; do not provoke me to anger by the works of your hands, and I shall not afflict you.’ But you did not listen to me,” says the Lord.

And somewhat later [XVIII]: “Cursed is the one who does the work of the Lord deceitfully.”

Again, somewhat later [Lamentations III]: “The Lord is good to those who hope in him, to the soul that seeks him. It is good to await the salvation of the Lord in silence. It is good for a man to bear the yoke from his youth. He shall sit alone and be silent, because he has lifted it upon himself” [Note: [Col. 0941] Thus the manuscripts, in accordance with the Vulgate in the uncorrupted Bibles. But the printed editions had, “he raised himself upon himself.”]. “He shall put his mouth in the dust, if perhaps there may be hope. He shall give his cheek to the one who strikes him; he shall be filled with reproaches, for the Lord will not reject forever.”

## From the Book of Ezekiel

[Chapter III] When seven days had passed, the word of the Lord came to me, saying: “Son of man, I have appointed you as a watchman for the house of Israel. You shall hear a word from my mouth and announce it to them from me. If, when I say to the wicked, ‘You shall surely die,’ you do not announce it to him, nor speak so that he may turn from his wicked way and live, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but I shall require his blood from your hand.

“But if you announce it to the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness and from his wicked way, he indeed shall die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life. And if the righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, I shall place a stumbling block before him; he shall die because you did not announce it to him. He shall die in his sin, and his righteousnesses that he performed shall not be remembered; but I shall require his blood from your hand.

“But if you announce to the righteous man that the righteous man must not sin, and he does not sin, he shall surely live, because you announced it to him, and you will have saved your life.”

And somewhat later [IX]: “And the Lord said to him: ‘Pass through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and mark a Tau upon the foreheads of the men who groan and grieve over all the abominations that are committed in its midst.’ And he said to the others, while I listened: ‘Pass through the midst of the city after him and strike; let your eye not spare, and do not have mercy. Kill old man, young man, virgin, little child, and women, even to destruction. But do not kill anyone upon whom you see the Tau; and begin from my sanctuary.’”

And somewhat later [XIII]: “Because you have falsely grieved the heart of the righteous, whom I did not grieve, and have strengthened the hands of the wicked so that he would not turn back from his evil way and live.”

Again, somewhat later [XVI]: “Behold, this was the iniquity of Sodom, your sister: pride, fullness of bread, abundance, and the leisure of her and her daughters; and they did not extend a hand to the needy and poor. They became proud and committed abominations before me, and I took them away, as you have seen.”

And shortly afterward [XVIII.]: If a man is righteous and practices judgment and righteousness; if he has not eaten upon the mountains, nor lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel; if he has not violated his neighbor’s wife, nor approached a menstruating woman; if he has not saddened anyone, has returned the debtor’s pledge, has taken nothing away by force; if he has given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with clothing; if he has not lent at interest, nor taken anything beyond what was due; if he has turned his hand away from wrongdoing and rendered true judgment between one man and another; if he has walked in my commandments and observed my judgments, so as to practice truth: he is righteous; he shall surely live, says the Lord God.

But if he fathers a son who is a robber and sheds blood, and does one of these things—and indeed does none of all these things, but eats upon the mountains and defiles his neighbor’s wife; who saddens the needy and the poor, commits robberies, and does not return a pledge; who lifts his eyes to idols and commits abominations; who lends at interest and takes more than is due—[Col. 0943] shall he live? He shall not live. Since he has done all these detestable things, he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him.

But if he fathers a son who, seeing all the sins of his father that he committed, fears and does not do anything like them; who does not eat upon the mountains and does not lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel; who does not violate his neighbor’s wife; who does not sadden anyone, does not retain a pledge, and does not commit robbery; who gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing; who turns his hand away from wronging the poor, and does not take interest or anything beyond what is due; who practices my judgments and walks in my commandments: he shall not die because of his father’s iniquity, but shall surely live.

His father, because he oppressed and used violence against his brother and did evil among his people—behold, he has died in his iniquity. And you say, “Why has the son not borne the iniquity of the father?” Clearly, because the son practiced judgment and righteousness; he observed and carried out all my commandments: he shall surely live.

The soul that sins shall itself die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, and the father shall not bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him.

But if the wicked man repents of all his sins that he has committed, and observes all my commandments, and practices judgment and righteousness, he shall surely live and shall not die. None of all his iniquities that he committed shall be remembered against him; he shall live because of the righteousness that he has practiced.

Is my will the death of the wicked, says the Lord God, and not rather that he should turn from his ways and live?

But if the righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity according to all the abominations that the wicked ordinarily commits, shall he live? None of all the righteous deeds that he had done shall be remembered. In the transgression by which he transgressed, and in the sin that he committed, in these he shall die.

And you said, “The way of the Lord is not fair.” Hear now, house of Israel: Is my way not fair, and are not your ways rather crooked? For when the righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, he shall die because of them; he shall die in the injustice that he has committed. And when the wicked man turns away from his wickedness that he has committed and practices judgment and righteousness, he shall preserve his life. For he has considered and turned away from all his iniquities that he committed; he shall surely live and shall not die.

And the children of Israel say, “The way of the Lord is not fair.” Are my ways not fair, house of Israel, and are not your ways rather crooked? Therefore I shall judge each one according to his ways, house of Israel, says the Lord God.

Turn, and repent of all your iniquities, and iniquity shall not become your ruin. Cast away from yourselves all your transgressions by which you have transgressed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, house of Israel? For I do not desire the death of the one who dies, says the Lord God. Return, and live.

[Note: [Col. 0943] The Royal codex has “and you shall live.”]

And somewhat later [XXII.]: Behold, the princes of Israel, each according to his own strength, were in you to shed blood. They treated father and mother with contempt among you; they oppressed the resident alien in your midst; they saddened the orphan and the widow among you. You despised my sanctuaries and profaned my Sabbaths.

[Note: [Col. 0944] So also in Jerome and in the Corbie manuscript Bibles. But in the printed Bibles: “you despised, and you profaned my Sabbaths.”]

Slanderers were among you, intent on shedding blood; and upon the mountains they ate among you: they committed wickedness in your midst. They uncovered their father’s nakedness among you; they humbled the impurity of a menstruating woman among you. Each man committed an abomination with his neighbor’s wife; and the father-in-law polluted his daughter-in-law shamefully; the brother oppressed his sister, his father’s daughter, among you. They accepted gifts among you in order to shed blood; you took interest and excess, and greedily oppressed your neighbors, while forgetting me, says the Lord God.

And shortly afterward: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, say to her, “You are an unclean land, and you have not been rained upon in the day of fury. There is a conspiracy of prophets in her midst. Like a roaring lion seizing prey, they have devoured a soul,

[Note: [Col. 0944] The Vulgate has “souls,” although the Corbie Bible has “a soul.”]

they have taken wealth and payment, and they have multiplied her widows in her midst. Her priests have despised my law and profaned my sanctuaries; they have made no distinction between the sacred and the profane, and they have not understood the difference between the polluted and the unclean.”

And two verses later: Her princes are in her midst like wolves seizing prey, intent on shedding blood, destroying lives, and greedily pursuing profit. But her prophets daubed them with plaster without tempering it, seeing vanities and divining lies, saying, “Thus says the Lord God,” when the Lord had not spoken. The people of the land practiced oppression and committed robbery; they afflicted the needy and the poor, and oppressed the resident alien with oppression, without judgment.

And I sought among them a man who might build a wall and stand in the breach before me on behalf of the land, so that I would not destroy it; but I found none. And I poured out my indignation upon them, and consumed them in the fire of my wrath. I repaid their way upon their own heads, says the Lord God.

And somewhat later [XXXIII.]: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, speak to the children of your people, and say to them: When I bring a sword upon a land, and the people of the land take one man from among their least members and appoint him as a watchman over them; and when he sees the sword coming upon the land, blows the trumpet, and announces it to the people; then whoever hears the sound of the trumpet, whoever he may be, and does not take heed, and the sword comes and takes him, his blood shall be upon his own head. He heard the sound of the trumpet and did not take heed; his blood shall be upon him. But if he had kept watch, he would have saved his life.

But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet, and the people do not take heed, and the sword comes and takes a life from among them, that man indeed has been taken in his iniquity; but I shall require his blood from the hand of the watchman.

[Col. 0945] And you, son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Therefore, hearing a word from my mouth, you shall announce it to them from me. If, when I say to the wicked man, “Wicked man, you shall surely die,” you do not speak so that the wicked man may guard himself from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but I shall require his blood from your hand. But if, when you announce to the wicked man that he should turn from his ways, he does not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity; but you have saved your life.

Therefore you, son of man, say to the house of Israel: Thus you have spoken, saying, “Our iniquities and our sins are upon us, and in them we waste away; how then can we live?” Say to them: “As I live, says the Lord God, I do not desire the death of the wicked, but that the wicked should return

[Note: [Col. 0945] In the Vulgate, “turn”; and a little later the word is repeated: “Turn, turn from [your] ways,” etc.]

from his evil way and live. Turn from your most evil ways; why should you die, house of Israel?”

Therefore you, son of man, say to the children of your people: The righteousness of the righteous man shall not deliver him on whatever day he sins, and the wickedness of the wicked man shall not harm him on whatever day he turns from his wickedness; and the righteous man shall not be able to live by his righteousness on whatever day he sins.

Even if I say to the righteous man, “You shall surely live,” and, trusting in his righteousness, he commits iniquity, all his righteous deeds shall be consigned to oblivion, and in the iniquity that he has committed, in that he shall die.

But if I say to the wicked man, “You shall surely die,” and he repents of his sin and practices judgment and righteousness; if that wicked man returns the pledge and restores what he has robbed, walks in the commandments of life, and does nothing unjust, he shall surely live and shall not die. None of the sins that he committed shall be counted against him. He has practiced judgment and righteousness; he shall surely live.

And the children of your people said: “The way of the Lord is not evenly balanced.” Yet their own way is unjust. For when the righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquities, he shall die because of them. And when the wicked man turns away from his wickedness and practices judgment and righteousness, he shall live by them.

And you say: “The way of the Lord is not straight.” I shall judge each one of you according to his ways, house of Israel.

And after forty-nine verses: And you, son of man, son of your people who

[Note: [Col. 0945] In all the manuscripts the pronoun “who” is lacking.]

speak about you beside the walls and at the doors of the houses, saying to one another, each man to his neighbor: “Come, and let us hear what word proceeds from the Lord.” And they come to you as though the people were entering; and my people sit before you, and they hear your words but do not do them, because they turn them into a song for their mouths, while their heart follows its greed.

And you are to them like a musical song

[Note: [Col. 0945] The Royal codex has “a song of musicians.”]

that is sung with a pleasant and sweet sound; they hear your words but do not do them.

[Note: [Col. 0945] The manuscripts have: “and they will hear your words, and they will not do them.”]

And when what has been foretold comes—for behold, it is coming—then they shall know that a prophet has been among them.

[XXXIV.]: The word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, prophesy concerning the shepherds of Israel; prophesy, and say to the shepherds: Thus says the Lord God: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who fed themselves! Are not flocks fed by shepherds? You ate the milk, clothed yourselves with the wool, and slaughtered what was fat,

[Note: [Col. 0946] The manuscripts have “you ate.”]

but you did not feed my flock. You did not strengthen what was weak; you did not heal what was sick; you did not bind up what was broken; you did not bring back what had been cast away; you did not seek what had perished. Rather, you ruled over them with harshness and power.

And my sheep were scattered because there was no shepherd; and they became food for all the beasts of the field, and were scattered. My flocks wandered over all the mountains and every high hill; my flocks were scattered over the whole face of the earth. And there was no one who sought them—there was, I say, no one who sought them.

Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord: As I live, says the Lord God, because my flocks have become plunder,

[Note: [Col. 0946] The Royal codex has “my flocks have been given over to plunder.”]

and my sheep have become food for all the beasts of the field because there was no shepherd—for the shepherds did not seek my flock, but the shepherds fed themselves and did not feed my flocks—therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I myself am against the shepherds, and I shall require my flock from their hand. I shall put an end to them, so that they may no longer feed the flock, and the shepherds may no longer feed themselves. I shall rescue my flock from their mouth, and it shall no longer be food for them.

And shortly afterward: But as for you, my flocks, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I judge between one animal and another, between rams and goats.

[Note: [Col. 0946] The manuscripts have “between a ram and a goat.”]

Was it not enough for you to feed upon good pasture? Indeed, you trampled the remnants of your pastures with your feet; and when you drank the purest water, you muddied what remained with your feet. And my sheep fed upon what had been trampled by your feet, and drank what your feet had muddied.

Therefore thus says the Lord God to them:

[Note: [Col. 0946] So also in Jerome and in the Corbie manuscript Bibles. But the printed editions of the Vulgate have “to you.”]

Behold, I myself judge between the fat animal and the lean; because you pushed with your sides and shoulders, and butted with your horns all the weak animals until you scattered them outside.

And shortly afterward [XLV.]: Thus says the Lord God: Let it be enough for you, princes of Israel. Abandon iniquity and robbery, practice judgment and righteousness, and separate your boundaries from my people, says the Lord God. You shall have a just balance and a just ephah, and a just bath [measure].

We have taken these passages from books that the Jews also hold to be canonical, in which we found certain things that suited this work. But those books too must not be omitted which are certainly known to have been written before the Savior’s coming, yet, although they are not received by the Jews, are nevertheless received by the Church of that same Savior.

Among these are two books commonly attributed by many to Solomon, on account, as I think, of a certain similarity of style. For all the more learned are in no doubt that they are not Solomon’s. Yet in the case of the one called *Wisdom*, it is not apparent who its author is.

[Note: [Col. 0947] Augustine did not speak this way about the author of this book in *On Christian Doctrine*, book 2, chapter 8, section 13; but when he compiled this *Speculum*, he had already abandoned the earlier opinion by which he had there asserted that the Book of Wisdom had been written by Jesus Sirach. Compare book 2 of the *Retractions*, chapter 4, as well as the note on the aforementioned passage of book 2 of *On Christian Doctrine*.]

But the fact that the other book, which we call *Ecclesiasticus*, was written by a certain Jesus, surnamed Sirach, is established among those who have read the whole book. From the Book of Wisdom, then, the following passages appeared suitable for this work.

## FROM THE BOOK OF WISDOM

[Chapter I.] Love righteousness, you who judge the earth. Think of the Lord in goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart. For he is found by those who do not test him, and he appears to those who have faith in him. For perverse thoughts separate from God, but tested virtue rebukes the foolish. For wisdom will not enter into a malevolent soul, nor dwell in a body subjected to sins.

For the holy Spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and will withdraw from thoughts that are without understanding; and it will be rebuked by the iniquity that comes upon it. For the spirit of wisdom is benevolent, and will not free the blasphemer

[Note: [Col. 0947] The Sacred Bibles have “the slanderer.”]

from his lips; for God is witness to his inmost parts, and the true examiner of his heart, and the hearer of his tongue.

For the spirit of the Lord has filled the inhabited world, and that which contains all things possesses knowledge of speech. Therefore the one who speaks unrighteous things cannot remain hidden, nor will the rebuking judgment pass him by. For there will be an inquiry into the thoughts of the wicked, and the hearing of his words will come to the Lord, for the rebuke of his iniquities. For the ear of jealousy hears all things, and the tumult of murmuring will not be concealed.

Therefore guard yourselves against murmuring, which is of no benefit, and refrain your tongue from slander; for an obscure answer

[Note: [Col. 0947] The Vulgate has “an obscure word.”]

will not go into emptiness. But the mouth that lies kills the soul.

And shortly afterward [III.]: Those who trust in him shall understand the truth, and the faithful shall abide with him in love, because grace and peace belong to his chosen. But the wicked shall receive correction according to what they have devised, those who have neglected righteousness

[Note: [Col. 0947] The Vulgate has “those who have neglected the righteous one”; in Greek: οἱ ἀμελήσαντες τοῦ δικαίου, “those who neglected the righteous one.”]

and have departed from the Lord. For unhappy is the one who rejects wisdom and discipline.

And six verses later: For blessed is the barren woman who is undefiled, who has not known a marriage-bed in transgression; she shall have fruit at the visitation of souls

[Note: [Col. 0947] The Carnutensis codex, in agreement with the Vulgate in the printed editions and in the Corbie manuscript Bibles, has “of holy souls.” “Holy” is absent from the Greek.]

and the eunuch who has not committed iniquity with his hands, nor conceived wicked thoughts against the Lord.

And somewhat later [VI.]: Hear therefore, kings, and understand; learn justice, judges of the ends of the earth.

[Note: [Col. 0947] The word “justice” is found neither in the Vulgate nor in the Greek.]

Give ear, you who rule over multitudes and take pride in throngs of nations. For power was given to you by the Lord, and authority by the Most High, who will examine your works and scrutinize your thoughts.

[Col. 0948] For although you were ministers of his kingdom, you did not judge rightly, nor observe the law of righteousness, nor walk according to God’s will. Terribly and swiftly he will appear to you, because the harshest judgment will be made against those who rule.

For mercy is granted to the lowly, but the powerful shall suffer powerful torments. For the Lord will not withhold his regard from anyone, nor will he respect anyone’s greatness, because he himself made both the small and the great, and he cares equally for all. But a stronger punishment awaits the stronger.

But to you, wicked kings,

[Note: [Col. 0948] The word “wicked” is absent from the Vulgate. In the Greek, instead of “kings,” there is τύραννοι, “tyrants.”]

are my words, so that you may learn wisdom and not fall away. For those who have kept righteousness righteously

[Note: [Col. 0948] The Vulgate has “just things justly”; in Greek: ὁσίως τὰ ὅσια, “holy things holily.”]

shall be justified, and those who have learned these things shall find what answer to give.

Therefore desire my words, love them, and you shall acquire discipline. For wisdom is radiant and never fades, and is easily seen by those who love her, and is found by those who seek her. She anticipates those who desire her, so that she may show herself to them first. Whoever keeps watch for her from the light of day will not labor; for he will find her sitting at his doors.

For thinking about her is perfect understanding, and whoever keeps watch for her will soon be secure. For she goes about seeking those who are worthy of her, and she shows herself to them graciously in their paths, and meets them in every providence.

For the beginning of her is the most genuine desire for discipline. Care for discipline is love, and love is the keeping of her laws; the keeping of her laws is the assurance

[Note: [Col. 0948] So in the printed editions and manuscripts, in agreement with the Greek, βεβαίωσις. But the Vulgate reads “completion.”]

of incorruption; and incorruption makes one near to God. Therefore desire for wisdom leads to an everlasting kingdom.

If, then, you delight in thrones and scepters, rulers of peoples, love wisdom, so that you may reign forever.

And shortly afterward [VIII.]: And if anyone loves righteousness, her labors possess great virtues. For she teaches sobriety and wisdom, righteousness and virtue, than which nothing is more useful in life to human beings.

Now what appear suitable are to be set forth from the book called *Ecclesiasticus*. Concerning this book, I think that I have also said here what I previously stated concerning the Book of Proverbs, although in this *Ecclesiasticus* I find more passages necessary for this work.

## FROM ECCLESIASTICUS

[Chapter I.] The fear of the Lord is the religiousness of knowledge. Religious devotion will guard and justify the heart; it will give gladness and joy. It shall be well with the one who fears the Lord, and he shall be blessed in the days of his completion. The fullness of wisdom is to fear God, and its fullness comes from its fruits.

And two verses later: The crown of wisdom is the fear of the Lord.

And four verses later: The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, for its branches are long-lived. In the treasuries of wisdom there is understanding, and religious devotion belongs to knowledge; but wisdom is an abomination to sinners.

The fear of the Lord drives out sin. For the one who is without fear cannot be justified.

[Note: [Col. 0949] The Vulgate has “will not be able to be justified.”]

For the anger of his indignation is his overthrow. The wise man

[Note: [Col. 0949] The word “wise” is absent from the Sacred Bibles.]

will endure patiently until the proper time, and afterward there will be a return of joy. Good sense will conceal his words for a time, and the lips of many will recount his understanding.

Desiring wisdom, preserve righteousness, and God will provide it for you. For wisdom and discipline are the fear of the Lord; and what is pleasing to him is faith and gentleness, and he will fill your treasures.

[Note: [Col. 0949] The Royal codex has “and he will fill your words.” The Vulgate has “and he will fill its treasures.”]

Do not be incredulous toward the fear of the Lord, and do not approach him with a divided heart. Do not be a hypocrite before human beings, and do not cause yourself to stumble by your lips. Pay attention to these things, lest you fall and bring confusion upon your soul; and lest God reveal your hidden things and strike you down in the midst of the assembly. For you have approached the Lord maliciously, and your heart is full of deceit and treachery.

[II.] My son, when you approach the service of God, stand in fear and righteousness, and prepare your soul for temptation. Humble your heart and endure. Incline your ear and receive the words of understanding, and do not hasten toward the time of ruin.

[Note: [Col. 0949] The Vulgate has “in the time”; in agreement with the Greek, ἐν καιρῷ, “at the proper time.”]

Endure the sustaining of God; cling to God, and endure, so that your life may increase at the end. Accept everything that is brought upon you, and endure in pain; in your humiliation have patience. For gold and silver are tested in fire, but acceptable human beings in the furnace of humiliation.

Believe in God, and he will restore you; direct your way and hope in him. Preserve his fear, and grow old in it. You who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy, and do not turn away from him, lest you fall. You who fear the Lord, believe in him, and your reward shall not be lost. You who fear the Lord, hope in him, and his mercy will come to you in delight.

[Note: [Col. 0949] The Vulgate has “into delight”; in agreement with the Greek, εἰς εὐφροσύνην, “into gladness.”]

You who fear God, love him, and your hearts shall be enlightened. Look upon the generations of human beings, children, and know: Who has hoped in the Lord and been put to shame?

[Note: [Col. 0949] So in the printed editions and manuscripts, in agreement with the Greek. But the Vulgate has “for no one who hoped,” and shortly afterward, “for who has remained,” and so forth.]

Who has remained in his commandments and been forsaken? And who has called upon him, and he has despised him? For God is gracious and merciful, and in the time of tribulation he will forgive the sins of all who seek him in truth.

Woe to the double-hearted,

[Note: [Col. 0949] The Vulgate has: “And he will forgive sins on the day of tribulation, and he is a protector of all who seek him,” and so forth. But the Greek text reads: “He forgives sins and saves in the time of tribulation. Woe to timid hearts.”]

and to deceitful lips, and to hands that do evil, and to the sinner who walks upon the earth by two paths. Woe to those who are fainthearted and do not believe God; therefore they are not protected by him. Woe to those who have lost endurance, who have abandoned straight ways and turned aside into crooked paths.

And what will you do when God begins to examine you?

Those who fear the Lord will not be incredulous toward his word, and those who love him will preserve his way.

[Col. 0950] Those who fear the Lord will seek what is pleasing to him, and those who love him will be filled with his law. Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts and sanctify their souls before him. Those who fear the Lord keep his commandments and will have patience until his visitation, saying: “If we do not repent, we shall fall into the hands of God, and not into the hands of human beings.” For according to his greatness, so also is his mercy with him.

[III.] The children of wisdom are the assembly of the righteous, and their nation is obedience and love. Hear the judgment of the father, beloved children,

[Note: [Col. 0950] The word “beloved” is absent from the printed Bibles; it is found in the ancient Corbie Bibles.]

and act accordingly, so that you may be saved.

And two verses later: Whoever loves God will make intercession for sins and will restrain himself from them; in the prayer of his days he shall be heard. And just as the one who treasures up, so also the one who honors his mother.

Whoever honors his father will rejoice in children. Whoever honors his father shall live a longer life, and whoever obeys his father will refresh his mother. Whoever fears God honors his parents, and will serve those who begot him as though they were masters.

In deed, word, and every kind of patience, honor your father, so that blessing may come upon you from the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0950] The Vulgate, in agreement with the Greek, has “from him.” In the written Corbie Bibles, however, it has “from God.”]

And three verses later: Do not glory in the dishonor of your father.

And three verses later: My son, support your father in his old age, and do not sadden him during his life. And if his understanding fails, grant him pardon, and do not despise him in your own strength.

And four verses later: How evil in reputation is the one who abandons his father! And accursed by God is the one who provokes his mother.

My son, complete your works in gentleness, and you will be loved more than human glory. The greater you are, humble yourself in all things, and you will find grace before God, because great is the power of God alone, and he is honored by the humble.

Do not seek what is higher than you, and do not investigate what is stronger than you; but always consider what God has commanded you, and do not be curious about many of his works. For it is not necessary for you to see with your eyes the things that are hidden.

[Note: [Col. 0950] The manuscripts have “it is not necessary for you to investigate the things that are hidden,” and omit “to see with your eyes.”]

And three verses later: For suspicion has misled many

[Note: [Col. 0950] This agrees well with the Greek, πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐπλάνησεν, “for it has led many astray.” The Vulgate, however, has “It has also tripped up many.” Yet in this same book, chapter 15, verse 12, the author of the Vulgate translates the verb ἐπλάνησεν as *implanavit*, that is, “deceived” or “led into error.”]

and held their minds in vanity. A hard heart will fare badly at the end, and whoever loves danger will perish in it. A heart that enters upon two paths shall have no success, and the perverse-hearted

[Note: [Col. 0950] The Royal manuscript has “of a perverse heart”; in agreement with the Vulgate in the printed editions, although the ancient Corbie Bibles have “perverse-hearted.”]

shall stumble in them. A wicked heart will be weighed down by sorrows, and the sinner will add sin to sin.

And two verses later: A wise heart is understood in wisdom, and a good ear will hear wisdom with every desire. A wise and understanding heart will abstain from sins, and shall have success in works of righteousness.

Water extinguishes a blazing fire, and almsgiving resists sins; and God, its observer,

[Note: [Col. 0951] We follow Erasmus, Lyon, Venice, and Louvain. In B., “your observer.” M.]

who repays grace, remembers it afterward.

[Note: [Col. 0951] The Vulgate has “He remembers it afterward.” “It” is absent from the Greek and from the Latin Corbie Bibles. Immediately afterward, all the Bibles read: “and in the time of his fall he will find support.”]

And in the time of your fall you will find support.

[IV.] My son, do not defraud the poor of alms, and do not turn your eyes away from the poor. Do not despise a hungry soul, and do not provoke the poor in his need. Do not afflict the heart of the needy, and do not delay giving to one in distress. Do not reject the plea of the afflicted, and do not turn your face away from the needy.

Do not avert your eyes from the poor because of anger, and do not leave those who ask you so that they may curse you afterward. For the prayer of the one who curses you in the bitterness of his soul will be heard. And the one who made him will hear him.

Make yourself approachable to the assembly of the poor, humble your soul before the elder, and bow your head before the great. Incline your ear to the poor without sadness, and repay your debt to him, and answer him peacefully and gently.

Deliver the one who suffers injury from the hand of the proud, and do not bear it bitterly in your soul. In judgment be merciful, like a father to orphans and like a husband to their mother; and you will be like an obedient son of the Most High, and he will have mercy on you more than a mother.

Wisdom has breathed life into her children, and she receives those who seek her and goes before them on the way of righteousness. Whoever loves her loves life, and those who keep watch for her shall embrace her delight.

[Note: [Col. 0951] The Royal codex has “they shall be filled with her sweetness.” The Greek text has ἐμπλησθήσονται εὐφροσύνης, “they shall be filled with gladness.”]

Those who hold fast to her shall inherit life, and wherever she enters, God will bless. Those who serve her shall obey the Holy One, and God loves those who love her. Whoever hears her judges the nations,

[Note: [Col. 0951] The Vulgate now has “will judge,” and shortly afterward, “in the establishment of his creation.” But in the ancient Corbie Bibles both passages agree with this *Speculum*.]

and whoever looks upon her shall remain confident. If he trusts in her, he shall inherit her, and their offspring shall be established.

For she walks with him in temptation, and at the beginning she chooses him. She will bring fear, dread, and testing upon him, and will torment him in the tribulation of her instruction, until she tests him in his thoughts and trusts his soul. Then she will strengthen him and lead him again

[Note: [Col. 0951] The manuscripts have “and will now lead him again.” The Greek reads καὶ πάλιν ἐπανέξει κατ’ εὐθεῖαν πρὸς αὐτόν, “and again she will return straight to him.”]

on a straight path toward him, and make him glad. She will reveal her secrets to him and store up for him knowledge and understanding of righteousness.

But if he goes astray, she will abandon him and hand him over to the power of his enemy.

My son, preserve your time, and avoid evil. For the sake of your life, do not be ashamed to speak the truth. For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that brings glory and grace.

Do not show partiality against your own person, nor lie against your own soul. Do not be ashamed of your neighbor in his misfortune, nor hold back a word at the time

[Note: [Col. 0951] The printed editions have “for the time.” But the manuscripts have “at the time,” in agreement with the Vulgate, which in the following verse, instead of “and instruction in words of truth,” prefers “and instruction in the word of the discerning.” The Greek text has ἐν ῥήματι γλώσσης, “in a word of the tongue.”]

of salvation. Do not conceal your wisdom in its beauty. For wisdom and understanding are recognized in the tongue, and knowledge and instruction in words of truth, and firmness in works of righteousness.

[Col. 0952] Do not contradict the truth in any way, and be ashamed of the lack of instruction in your falsehood. Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not subject yourself to anyone so as to sin. Do not resist the powerful face, nor strive against the force of the river.

[Note: [Col. 0952] So in the manuscripts, in agreement with the Greek and the Vulgate. But the printed editions had “the force of lightning.”]

Fight for your soul in righteousness, and contend for righteousness even unto death; and God will fight down your enemies for you.

Do not be hasty with your tongue, nor useless and lax in your works. Do not be like a lion in your house, overturning your household and oppressing those subject to you. Let your hand not be extended for taking, and clenched for giving.

### [V.]

Do not pay attention to unjust possessions, and do not say, “I have enough for life.” For nothing will profit you at the time of vengeance and retribution. Do not follow the desire of your heart [Note: The Vulgate has: “Do not follow the desire of your heart in your strength.”], and do not say, “How could I?” or, “Who will subject me because of my deeds?” For God will indeed take vengeance. And do not say, “I have sinned, and what sorrowful thing has happened to me?” For the Most High is a patient requiter.

Do not be without fear concerning the propitiation of sins [Note: In the Latin Bibles, “concerning the propitiated sin.” In the Greek text, *peri exilasmou*, “concerning propitiation,” with the word “sins” omitted.]; nor add sin upon sin. And do not say, “The mercy of God is great; he will have mercy on the multitude of my sins.” For mercy and wrath quickly draw near from him, and his wrath looks upon sinners.

Do not delay turning to the Lord, and do not put it off from day to day. For his wrath will come suddenly, and at the time of vengeance he will destroy you. Do not be anxious about unjust riches, for they will profit you nothing on the day of retribution and vengeance.

Do not toss yourself about in every wind, and do not go along every road [Note: Thus the printed editions and manuscripts, in agreement with the Greek. But the Vulgate has, “in every wind . . . in every way.”]. For in this way the sinner is tested by a double tongue. Be steadfast in the way of God, and in the truth of your understanding and knowledge; and let the word of peace and justice accompany you.

Be gentle in hearing the word of God, so that you may understand; and with wisdom give [Note: The Regius manuscript has *fer*, “bear.” The Greek has *phtheggou*. The Vulgate has “bring forth.”] a true answer. If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, let your hand be over your mouth, lest you be caught by an undisciplined word and be put to shame.

Honor and glory belong to a person of understanding in speech; but the tongue of the imprudent is his own downfall. Do not be called a whisperer during your life, and do not be caught by your tongue and put to shame. For shame, repentance, and the worst reproach are upon the thief and the double-tongued; but upon the whisperer come hatred, enmity, and insult.

Justify the small and the great alike.

### [VI.]

Do not become an enemy to your neighbor on account of a friend. For the wicked will inherit reproach and insult, and every sinner is envious and double-tongued. Do not exalt yourself in the thought of your soul like a bull, lest your strength be shattered through folly.

And after seven verses:

Let many be at peace with you; but let one out of a thousand be your counselor. If you possess a friend, possess him in testing, and do not readily entrust yourself to him [Note: The word “yourself” is absent from the sacred Bibles.]. For there is a friend according to his own time, and he will not remain on the day of tribulation. There is also a friend who turns [Note: The Vulgate has “who turns himself”] toward enmity; and there is a friend who will expose hatred, strife, and insults.

There is also a friend who is a table-companion, and he will not remain on the day of need. If a friend remains steadfast, he will be to you like an equal, and he will act confidently among your household. If he humbles himself before you and hides himself from your face, you will have a united and good friendship.

Separate yourself from your enemies, and pay attention to your friends. A faithful friend is a strong protection; whoever finds him has found a treasure. Nothing compares with a faithful friend, and gold and silver are not worth weighing against the goodness of his faithfulness. A faithful friend is a medicine of life and immortality; and those who fear the Lord will find him.

Whoever fears God will have a good friendship in equal measure, for his friend will be like him.

My son, receive instruction from your youth, and you will find wisdom even into old age. Approach it like one who plows and sows, and endure its good fruits. For you will labor little at its work, and soon you will eat of its produce.

How exceedingly harsh wisdom is to the uneducated, and the senseless person will not remain in it [Note: The manuscripts have “remains.”]. It will be to them like the strength of a stone as a test, and they will not delay casting it away.

And after two verses:

But for those who have recognized it, it remains [Note: The printed editions have “they remain.” The manuscripts, in agreement with the Vulgate, have “it remains.”] until the sight of God.

Listen, my son, and accept the counsel of understanding, and do not reject my counsel. Put your foot into its fetters and your neck into its collar. Submit your shoulder and carry it, and do not become weary of its bonds. Approach it with all your soul, and with all your strength keep its ways. Search it out, and it will be revealed to you; and having become steadfast, do not abandon it. For in the end you will find rest in it, and it will be turned for you into delight. Its fetters will be for you a protection of strength and foundations of might, and its collar a robe of glory.

And after four verses:

My son, if you pay attention to me, you will learn [Note: The printed editions have “you will learn it.” The word “it” is absent from the manuscripts of this book and from the more reliable Bibles.]; and if you apply your soul, you will be wise. If you incline your ear, you will receive instruction; and if you love hearing, you will be wise.

Stand among a multitude of prudent elders, and join yourself wholeheartedly to their wisdom, so that you may be able to hear every account of God, and so that sayings of praise may not escape you. If you see a person of understanding, rise early to go to him, and let your foot wear down the steps of his doors.

Keep the commandments of God in your thoughts, and be especially constant in his precepts; and he himself will give you a heart, and the desire for wisdom will be given to you.

### [VII.]

Do not do evil, and evils will not seize you. Depart from injustice, and evils will withdraw from you. Do not sow evil in the furrows of injustice, and you will not reap it sevenfold.

Do not seek leadership from a man [Note: Thus also in the ancient Corbeiensis Bibles. But the printed Vulgate now has “from the Lord,” in agreement with the Greek *para Kyriou*.], nor a seat of honor from a king. Do not justify yourself before God, for he himself knows the heart; and do not desire to appear wise before a king.

Do not seek to become a judge unless you are able by your strength to break through iniquities [Note: Earlier editions had “to break through the strength of iniquity.” We have corrected this according to the manuscripts, which agree with the Vulgate.], lest you be terrified by the face of the powerful and place a stumbling-block in your own agility [Note: The Vulgate had this reading in the ancient Corbeiensis and in most other Bibles; but it has been replaced by “in your equity,” in agreement with the Greek *en euthutēti sou*.].

Do not sin against the multitude of the city, and do not thrust yourself into the crowd. Do not bind together double sins, for you will not be innocent in one of them. Do not be fainthearted in your soul. Do not neglect to entreat and to give alms.

Do not say, “The Lord will look upon me because of the multitude of my gifts, and when I offer to God Most High, he will accept my offerings.”

Do not mock a person in the bitterness of his soul, for there is a God who humbles and exalts [Note: The Vulgate has “a God who observes and exalts.”]. Do not plow falsehood against your brother, nor do the same to a friend. Do not desire to utter every falsehood, for its constant repetition is not good [Note: The Regius manuscript has “is not good,” omitting “is”; so also the Corbeiensis Bible. Moreover, the Greek reads *ouk eis agathon*, “not for good.”].

Do not be talkative in the assembly of elders.

And after twelve verses:

Do not harm a servant who works faithfully, nor a hired worker who gives his life. Let a sensible servant be beloved by you as your own soul. Do not defraud him of his freedom, nor leave him destitute.

And after two verses:

Do you have sons? Instruct them, and bend them from their childhood. Do you have livestock? Pay attention to them [Note: This passage must be restored according to the Vulgate, in which verse 24 reads: “Do you have livestock? Pay attention to them, and if they are useful, let them remain with you.” Then verse 25 follows: “Do you have sons?” and so forth.]. Do you have daughters? Guard their bodies, and do not show them a cheerful face.

Give your daughter in marriage, and you will have accomplished a great work; and give her to a sensible man. If you have a wife according to your soul, do not cast her away; and do not entrust yourself wholeheartedly to one who is hateful.

Honor your father, and do not forget your mother’s groaning. Remember that, unless it were through them, you would not have been born [Note: The word “born” is absent from the manuscripts of the *Speculum* and from the ancient Corbeiensis Bibles.]; and repay them as they also repaid you.

Fear God with your whole soul, and sanctify his priests. Love with all your strength the God [Note: The sacred Bibles have “love him who made you.”] who made you, and do not abandon his ministers. Honor God with your whole soul, and honor the priests.

And after six verses:

Stretch out your hand to the poor, so that your blessing may be completed [Note: The Vulgate has “your propitiation and blessing.” The word “propitiation” is absent from the Greek text.]. A grace given [Note: The Vulgate has “of those who are given”; and shortly afterward “and to the dead,” omitting the preposition “from,” with which the Regius manuscript of the *Speculum* agrees in these passages.] in the sight of every living person; and do not withhold grace from the dead.

Do not fail those who weep in consolation [Note: The manuscripts of this work have “in supplication.”], and walk with those who mourn.
